# discord_guild_welcome_screen (Resource)

Manages a community guild's welcome screen. The object always exists for community guilds; deleting this resource leaves it unchanged.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "discord_guild_welcome_screen" "main" {
  guild_id    = "123456789012345678"
  enabled     = true
  description = "Welcome to our community!"

  welcome_channels = [
    {
      channel_id  = "111111111111111111"
      description = "Read the rules"
      emoji_name  = "📜"
    },
    {
      channel_id  = "222222222222222222"
      description = "Introduce yourself"
      emoji_name  = "👋"
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `guild_id` (String) Snowflake ID of the guild. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `description` (String) The server description shown on the welcome screen.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the welcome screen is enabled. Write-only: Discord does not return this on read.
- `welcome_channels` (Attributes List) Up to 5 channels shown on the welcome screen. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--welcome_channels))

<a id="nestedatt--welcome_channels"></a>
### Nested Schema for `welcome_channels`

Required:

- `channel_id` (String) Snowflake ID of the channel.
- `description` (String) Description shown for the channel.

Optional:

- `emoji_id` (String) Snowflake ID of a custom emoji shown for the channel.
- `emoji_name` (String) Unicode emoji or custom emoji name shown for the channel.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Welcome screens are imported using the guild ID.
terraform import discord_guild_welcome_screen.main 123456789012345678
```
